title: Introduce probe arbiter priority index and shortfall escrow
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Adds a probe arbiter service and a probe priority index to improve probe allocation under constrained budgets; introduces a shortfall escrow that stores rollback credits for under-sampled cohorts. Includes new metrics and dashboards; safe rollout by default.
description: Context: Canary probes are our primary signal for detecting regressions, but high-cardinality and bursty traffic cause probe starvation in some cohorts while others are oversampled. Motivation: reduce missed regressions and noisy false positives caused by uneven probe distribution, without increasing overall probe budget. Design: introduce a lightweight 'probe arbiter' that centralizes short-lived probe decisions. The arbiter maintains a priority index per cohort that combines recent drift score, historic coverage, and probe shortfall debt. When global probe budget is constrained the arbiter favors cohorts with high drift and high shortfall debt. A shortfall escrow mechanism allocates rollback-credit tokens to cohorts that missed probes; tokens can be spent to temporarily elevate priority on subsequent windows, ensuring cohorts eventually catch up. Changes in this PR: 1) new service: perf/canary/arbiter (golang) - core allocation logic and metrics exporter; 2) controller changes to query arbiter before scheduling probes; 3) probe scheduler update to respect escrow tokens and priority index; 4) new Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards (canary/arbiter-overview, canary/shortfall-heatmap); 5) tests: unit + integration harness that simulates bursty traffic and sparse cohorts. Rollout plan: feature gated behind canary.allocator.v2; gradual ramp (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated monitoring checks for probe availability and false positive rate. If the false positive rate rises by >2x or coverage drops for critical cohorts, automatic rollback triggers. Backwards compatibility: arbiter serves as advisory; existing scheduler can be fallback if arbiter becomes unreachable. Testing: unit tests cover allocation heuristics and token accounting; integration test runs a 24h synthetic traffic replay validating allocation fairness and regression detection F1 score improvement. Impact: better detection coverage for long-tail cohorts and fewer wasted probes on stable cohorts.

notes: Performance: small CPU overhead on controller (~1-2% p95) observed during integration run.
Operational: arbiter is horizontally scalable and stateless; token state kept in compact kv with TTL to bound storage.
